easy.question: In Spring Lecture #21: Spring Boot Interceptors, what is the primary role of 'Syntax & rules of Spring Boot Interceptors' (demonstrated in InterceptorDemoApplication)?
options: It defines standard, compile-time verified semantics ensuring clean execution of Spring Boot Interceptors.
It is an obsolete construct that leads to unhandled hardware faults.
It converts all variables to global unmanaged primitives.
It bypasses class loading and executes purely as C binary code.
easy.explanation: In Spring Lecture #21: Spring Boot Interceptors, understanding 'Syntax & rules of Spring Boot Interceptors' is essential for mastering the core rules and syntax of Spring Boot Interceptors.

medium.question: During the execution of 'Design & architectural pattern of Spring Boot Interceptors' within main(), how does the runtime manage memory and object references?
options: By maintaining distinct stack frames for method calls and allocating objects on the heap with proper reference management.
By permanently locking CPU cache lines and preventing any garbage collection pass.
By converting local variables into ThreadLocal singletons without lifecycle bounds.
By discarding return values and relying strictly on system standard out.
medium.explanation: Runtime execution for Spring Boot Interceptors relies on structured heap allocation, stack frames, and clean object scoping.
medium.concept: Design & architectural pattern of Spring Boot Interceptors

hard.question: Under extreme production load (50,000 requests/sec), how should 'Boundary conditions & defensive checks in Spring Boot Interceptors' be designed to avoid bottlenecks?
options: By minimizing object allocations, avoiding lock contention, and implementing bounded resource pools with defensive timeouts.
By placing synchronized monitor locks across all public methods in the application.
By disabling all database connection pooling and creating new sockets per request.
By ignoring all exceptions and returning null values to prevent thread delays.
hard.explanation: Scalable backend architectures must balance memory allocation overhead, lock-free/low-contention concurrency, and resilient failure isolation.
hard.concept: Boundary conditions & defensive checks in Spring Boot Interceptors
